erin_cs: Heads-up: BlueWave onboarding - they see sporadic 429 spikes right after SDK init. Low steady traffic otherwise, but every few minutes a short burst of 20-40 429s for a few seconds. Help?

matt_eng: Do we have logs/headers from their requests? 429 body + any x-ratelimit headers would help.

kelsey_support: I grabbed a snippet from their repro session:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-ratelimit: 60;window=60
Body: {"error":"rate_limit","message":"too many preflight requests"}

They said bursts happen right after users hit the app home page.

alex_se: Sounds like preflight fanout / concurrent preflight from the browser SDK. Are they using the browser SDK with ephemeral tokens + per-tab init?

erin_cs: Yes browser SDK, ephemeral tokens via our sequence: page load -> fetch ephemeral -> sdk.init() -> immediate calls to embeddings + chat.setup.

matt_eng: Two likely culprits: (1) parallel preflight requests on init, (2) ephemeral token refresh causing short bump. Any chance their app is instantiating SDK multiple times per navigation?

kelsey_support: They confirmed single init, but they have a background worker that probes endpoints on load (analytics + feature flags) - could cause 3 concurrent early calls.

alex_se: Quick mitigation to try on their side: debounce initial calls and enable SDK option to serialize preflight. Example patch for the browser SDK:

// pseudo
const client = new RWSDK({
  preflight: { concurrency: 1, debounceMs: 75 }
});

That prevents multiple parallel preflight handshakes and spaces them out.

matt_eng: Also tell them to set `keepAlive: true` on their ephemeral token fetcher to reduce jitter when the token rotates. If token rotation coincides with user home load, that can double the handshake traffic.

erin_cs: I suggested both. They deployed the debounce change to staging and saw the bursts disappear in the next 10min window. Reporting back now. (thumbsup)

ratebot: rate-limiter alert: triggered 1m spike window at 3123457120 - peak 38 reqs/s, source group: browser-sdk:init.

kelsey_support: Nice. Can we surface a recommended default in the quickstart so new customers don't hit this? Most of our onboarding hits are browser-heavy.

alex_se: Yeah - recommend `preflight.concurrency:1` and `debounceMs:50-100` for browser SDKs in the quickstart under "Init best practices". Also add note about background probes and CI bots that can amplify.

matt_eng: I'll open a tiny docs PR and add a sample snippet + short troubleshooting checklist (check x-rw-ratelimit, verify single sdk.init, inspect token refresh timing).

erin_cs: BlueWave confirmed staging stayed healthy. They'll roll to prod tomorrow. I'll reopen if anything else. Thanks all.

kelsey_support: Leaving a short playbook entry in onboarding checklist: "If early 429s, try preflight serialization + 50-100ms debounce, avoid concurrent init calls."

matt_eng: Added. PR link: https://redwood.in/docs/sdk-init-rate-debounce (will update with real path after review).

erin_cs: Closing thread for now.
